MEMORANDUM

  Agenda Item #: __3___
  Meeting Date: January 23, 2018

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

THRU:  ANTON DAHLERBRUCH, CITY MANAGER /s/

FROM:  SHERI REPP-LOADSMAN, DEPUTY CITY MANAGER/PLANNING &
  BUILDING DIRECTOR /s/

SUBJECT: CONSIDERATION OF PARKLANDS COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATIONS
  OF JANUARY 11, 2018

DATE:  JANUARY 23, 2018

ISSUE/PURPOSE

The purpose of this memorandum is to transmit Parklands Committee recommendations from the
January 11, 2018 meeting to the City Council.

BACKGROUND/DISCUSSION

At its meeting of January 11, 2018 the Parklands Committee reviewed and discussed 6 applications
for tree removals, one applications in Parklands for retention of private plantings, one application for
a topping of trees, 2 application for a waiver of planting of the Designated Street Tree and one Final
Plan for a Change To Parklands as follows:

A. PC-482-17; Application to remove 1 New Zealand Christmas tree located in the parkway
  adjacent to 2736 Paseo Del Mar

  Applicant:  Lori O’Hern
  2736 Paseo Del Mar
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Page 1 of 7
 Staff introduced this application as a request to remove one New Zealand Christmas tree to improve
the view for their neighbor. The committee agreed the nonconforming tree significantly encroached
into the neighbors view, was not the neighborhood character and did not need to be replaced with
another tree since Kentia palms had been recently planted at the subject property in compliance with
a previous requirement to plant the designated street trees.

Committee member Kaviani motioned second by Rubincam to recommend to City Council approval
of PC-482-17, to remove 1 New Zealand Christmas tree located in the parkway according to the
Standard Conditions For Tree Removal Approvals. Payment of $500 to the Tree Bank and removal
of the stump are required. The vote was (4-0-1, in favor, Richie-Bray absent).

B. PC-485-18; Application to remove one American Elm tree located in the parkway adjacent to 448
  Via Media

  Applicant:  Jennifer Brown
  448 Via Media
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application as a request to improve the view by removing one American Elm
in the parkway located adjacent to 448 Via Media. The Committee members all agreed the tree was
a significant obstruction from all rooms in the home and was no longer the neighborhood character
but should be replaced with two designated street trees. Additional discussion centered on requiring
a payment to the Tree Bank as mitigation for the loss of a City street tree.

Committee member Leach motioned second by Rubincam to recommend to City Council approval
of PC-485-18, to remove one American Elm tree located in the parkway adjacent to 448 Via Media
according to the Standard Conditions For Tree Removal approvals. Mitigation payment of $500 to
the ‘Tree Bank’ for removal of the American Elm and removal of the stump are required. Payment
of $1000 to the Tree Bank for the planting of 2 Little Gem Magnolias on Via Media and payment of
$500 to Tree Bank as mitigation for removal of a tree.. The vote was (4-0-1, in favor, Richie-Bray
absent).

After the discussion and motion on the next application, the Committee questioned the consistency
of the action for PC-485-18 and requested to reconsider for more discussion.

Committee member Leach motioned second by Rubincam to reconsider the action for PC-485-18.
The vote was (4-0-1, in favor, Richie-Bray absent).

The Committee understood that a payment to the Tree Bank for the loss of a street tree and payment
for the planting of one or more trees to promote the renewal of the urban forest was within their
authority but indicated that requiring both should be restricted to cases where a significant tree is
being removed.

Committee member Leach motioned second by Rubincam to recommend to City Council approval
of PC-485-18, to remove one American Elm tree located in the parkway adjacent to 448 Via Media
according to the Standard Conditions for Tree Removal Approvals. Payment of $1,000 to the ‘Tree

  Page 2 of 7
 Bank’ for the planting of two Little Gem Magnolias on Via Media and removal of the stump are
required. The vote was (4-0-1, in favor, Richie-Bray absent).

C. PC-486-18; Application to remove one Japanese black pine located in the parkway adjacent to
  353 Palos Verdes Drive West

  Applicant:  Ravi Sreerama
  353 Palos Verdes Drive West
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 902740

Staff introduced this as a request to remove one pine tree that was out of character with the
neighborhood. The Committee agreed the tree was not the neighborhood character and was no
longer attractive due to excessive trimming. The Committee indicated the tree should be removed
and a new street tree should be planted with a payment to the Tree Bank but a mitigation payment
for a degraded tree was not appropriate.

Committee member Kaviani motioned second by Rubincam to recommend to City Council approval
of PC-486-18, to remove one Japanese Black pine tree located in the parkway adjacent to 353 Palos
Verdes Drive West according to the Standard Conditions For Tree Removal Approvals. Payment of
$500 to the Tree Bank and removal of the stump are required. The vote was (3-1-1, in favor, Leach
dissenting, Richie-Bray absent).

D. PC-487-18; Application to retain 2 fruit trees located in the Parklands adjacent to 2912 Via
  De La Guerra

  Applicant:  Christopher Moerman
  2912 Via De La Guerra
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

The application requested approval to retain 2 fruit trees located in the Parklands for privacy. A Real
Property Records Report was requested at the time of sale which identified a number of
encroachments that were required to be removed. A majority of the Committee thought the 2 trees
were close enough to the property line to not be a barrier to public access and added beauty to the
Parklands. One member indicated the trees were not native and contrary to the Parklands Use Policy
and policy for private plantings in the Parklands.

Committee member Kaviani motioned second by Rubincam to recommend to City Council approval
of PC -487-18, to retain two fruit trees located in the Parkway adjacent to 2912 Via De La Guerra.
A legal contract between the City and the property owner defining a maintenance schedule and
standards that runs with the property in perpetuity are required. The vote was (2-1-1-1, in favor,
Wade dissenting, Leach abstain and Richie-Bray absent).

E. PC-488-18; Application to remove 3 Canary Island pine trees located in the parkway adjacent to
  1609/1613 Via Zurita

  Applicant:  Yelena and Boris Gelman
  1608 Via Zurita
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Page 3 of 7
 Committee member Rubincam motioned seconded by Kaviani to continue the application to allow a
survey to determine ownership of the trees. The vote was (4-0-1 in favor, Richie-Bray absent).

F. PC-489-18; Application for a waiver of planting the Designated Street Treeadjacent to 2440 Via
  Anacapa

  Applicant;  Sally Young
  2440 Via Anacapa
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application as a request to waive the requirements to plant street trees adjacent
to the property at 2440 Via Anacapa. The Committee understood the applicant is concerned that
there may not be appropriate planting locations. The Committee discussed the construction of a gas
line and 4 drain lines installed in or near the areas that could support a tree. The Committee discussed
the potential for property owners to defeat the requirement to plant street trees by not being mindful
to protect adequate locations for future planting and that the location of street trees should be
identified during the design process. Staff advised that two locations appeared to be feasible and the
drain lines could be relocated if necessary. The Committee noted that trees should not be planted if
the drains could not be or there was a potential safety issue due to proximity to the gas line. Staff
advised that the property owner was seeking to complete construction and a continuance for two
months could be a hardship.

Committee member Rubincam motioned seconded by Kaviani to recommend denial to the City
Council of PC-489-18, an application to waive the planting of the Designation Street Tree unless it
is determined by the Director and Urban Forester that the tree(s) cannot be planted safely in which
case, the waiver will be administratively authorized and the Parklands Committee will be advised of
the findings. The vote was (4-0-1 in favor, Richie-Bray absent).

G. PC-490-18; Application for a waiver of planting the ‘Designated Street Tree’ adjacent to 504
  Paseo Del Mar

  Applicant:  Mark Paullin
  504 Paseo Del Mar
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application as a request to waive the planting of the street trees adjacent to 504
Paseo Del Mar. The applicant installed the designated street trees as specimen palms and determined
they were obstructing the view. The palms were removed and this application submitted. The
Committee agreed the palms would encroach into the view and an in lieu payment for street trees for
address 500 through 601 Paseo Del Mar was an option previously approved.

Committee member Leach motioned seconded by Rubincam to recommend approval to the City
Council to waive the planting of the Designated Street Tree adjacent to 504 Paseo Del Mar. Payment
of $2000 to the ‘Tree Bank’ for the 4 trees waived is required. The vote was (4-0-1 in favor, Richie-
Bray absent).

  Page 4 of 7
 H. PC-491-18; Application to top 2 Peruvian pepper trees located in the parkway adjacent to
  1712 and 1716 Palos Verdes Drive West

  Applicant:  John and Feng Readyhoff
  1705 Via Boronada
  Palos Verdes Estates, Ca 90274

Staff introduced this item as an application to top 2 Peruvian pepper trees. The trees were previously
topped and the applicant requested approval to maintain these two tree so their view of the neighbor’s
roof tops were visible. Staff advised the previous topping was inconsistent with current tree
maintenance standards. The Committee agreed they could approve the application but were
concerned with how they could condition the trimming so as to not top the trees but trim and reduce
the trees in an attractive manner.

Committee member Leach motioned seconded by Kaviani to recommend approval to the City Council
to reduce the height of the trees adjacent to 1712 and 1716 Palos Verdes Drive West to 22-23 feet
above grade with an annual no-fee permit, issued to a qualified contractor at the applicant’s
responsibility, at the direction of the Urban Forester. The vote was (4-0-1 in favor, Richie-Bray
absent).

Staff advised the Parklands Committee and applicant that the annual no fee permit would no longer
be applicable upon the City Council approval of a tree trimming permit fee. Staff advised that the
applicant could obtain a no fee permit prior to March 11, 2018 when the new fee would be
implemented.

I. PC-CTP-07-16; Final planting plan to restore a portion of Parklands located adjacent to 990
  Paseo La Cresta

  Applicant:  Jason and Wendy Moskowitz
  990 Paseo La Cresta
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application as the Final Plan for a Change to Parklands application that has been
in the cue for an extended period of time. The Committee agreed the matter needed to be completed.
The members agreed the plants were good but the landscape unduly restricted the public’s access to
the large pine tree located along the hillside edge. The Committee discussed requiring a 10 feet wide
area to be unplanted for allow for access. The Committee indicated the applicant has not completed
the initial approval and should not proceed until all encroachment have been removed.

Committee member Wade motioned seconded by Leach to recommend approval of PC-CTP-07-16,
a Final Plan to restore a portion of Parklands located adjacent to 990 Paseo La Cresta with native
plants with the added conditions requiring all encroachments identified by the Parklands Committee
and City Council are removed as a condition precedent before any work is done and a ten foot wide
path marked on the plan is required to provide for public access to the tree and retaining wall. The
vote was (4-0-1 in favor, Richie-Bray absent).

J. PC-492-18; Application to remove 1 Deodar Cedar and 1 Aleppo pine located  in  the
  parkway adjacent to 537 Via Del Monte

  Page 5 of 7
   Applicant:  Jim Dutton
  536 Via Del Monte
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this as a view application. The Deodar Cedar was originally a small Christmas tree
that was planted by the property owner. Both this tree and the Allepo pine were noted to impact
views.

Committee member Leach motioned seconded by Rubincam to recommend approval to the City
Council to remove one Deodar Cedar and one Aleppo pine tree located in the parkway adjacent to
537 Via Del Monte according to the Standard Conditions for Tree Removal Approvals. Payment of
$1,000 to the Tree Bank for the planting of 2 Little Gem Magnolias trees at the Urban Forester’s
direction and removal of the stumps are required. The vote was (4-0-1 in favor, Richie-Bray absent).

K. PC-493-18; Application to remove 1 Italian Stone pine located in the parkway adjacent to
  1332 Via Gabriel

  Applicant:  Alan Haven
  2400 Via Sobrante
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Applicant:  Robert Moest
  2530 Wilshire Boulevard, 2nd floor
  Santa Monica, CA 90274

Staff introduced this as a view application and advised that the applicant was not present and a
presentation was available. Four residents spoke in opposition to the application. The Committee
discussed the prior authorizations that allowed the Italian Stone pine to be trimmed. Several
Committee members noted that there would not be a significant enhancement by removal of the tree
due to other trees obstructing the view. The Chairman stated removal of the tree would restore some
view, noted that other mature and beautiful trees have been removed and that his opinion has remained
consistent with the review of past applications..

Committee member Rubincam motioned seconded by Kaviani to recommend denial to the City
Council of PC-493-18, an application to remove one Italian Stone pine tree located in the parkway
adjacent to 1332 Via Gabriel. The vote was (3-1-1 in favor, Wade dissenting, Richie-Bray absent).

NOTIFICATION

Interested parties attending the Parklands Committee meeting were made aware that the above
noted recommendations would be transmitted to the City Council. This item is also noticed in
the standard manner for City Council meetings.

  Page 6 of 7
 RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council take the following actions:

1. Review and approve the Parklands Committee Recommended Actions of January 11,
  2018.
